summary: The December 20 session is a relief bounce, not a trend reversal. The cooler Nov PCE (2.4% vs 2.5% expected) provides genuine catalyst for the bounce, as it pushes back on the 'inflation re-acceleration' narrative that drove the hawkish Fed reaction. However, the structural reality is fewer 2025 rate cuts and higher-for-longer rates. Triple witching will dominate intraday price action with $6.6T in options expiring. Government shutdown noise adds headline volatility but limited fundamental impact. Rotation regime is confirmed — breadth remains weak (Dow 10-day losing streak just ended) while mega-cap tech holds up. Airlines and travel/leisure are the momentum leaders. Expect choppy, volatile session with upward bias in first half followed by OPEX-driven chaos in the final hour. The S&P at 5,930 faces resistance at 6,000 and support at 5,850.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.content: Government shutdown crisis dominates. On Dec 19, the House rejected Trump-backed GOP funding bill 174-235, with 38 Republicans defecting. Elon Musk spearheaded opposition to bipartisan deal on X. Government funding expires end of Friday Dec 20. Trump demands debt ceiling suspension through Jan 2027 plus $110B disaster relief. Partial shutdown risk elevated heading into holidays, though markets historically shrug off shutdowns within days. Geopolitical risk otherwise low — no major international escalation.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: CRITICAL: Nov PCE (released morning of Dec 20) came in at 2.4% YoY, below the 2.5% consensus, providing relief after the hawkish Fed shock. Core PCE at 2.8% in line. This is the key catalyst for today's rebound. Fed cut 25bps on Dec 18 to 4.25-4.50% but dot plot slashed 2025 rate cut expectations from 4 cuts to just 2 (3.75-4.00% year-end 2025). SEP raised core PCE forecast to 2.5% from 2.1% and GDP growth to 2.1%. 10Y yield at 4.52%, 2-10 spread positive at 19bps. Dollar index 107.62 retreating 0.73% after sharp post-Fed rally. USD/JPY surging to 157.64 (+1.92%) as BoJ held rates. S&P had worst Fed-day performance on record Wed (-2.95%), Dow on 10-day losing streak (worst since 1974). Today is OPEX/triple witching with ~$6.6T notional options expiring — largest event of 2024.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: Micron (MU) crashed 16% on Dec 19 after reporting weak Q2 guidance ($7.9B rev vs $8.98B expected, $1.43 EPS vs $1.91 expected). NAND oversupply, consumer demand weakness, and data center SSD demand pause cited. Broadcom (AVGO) still digesting blowout earnings from Dec 12 (revenue +44% YoY to $51.6B, AI revenue +220% to $12.2B). Airlines strong — UAL +4.5%, DAL +2.6%, BA +2.6% on Dec 19 close. Cruise lines rallied (CCL +1.5%, NCLH +1.2%). Boeing rebounding from operational lows. UNH down 2.1% continuing post-CEO-assassination weakness.

sections.title: Tech
sections.content: Semiconductor bifurcation: AI-exposed names (NVDA, AVGO) holding up while broader semi complex weakens (MU -16%, AMD -2.1%). SMH at 238.87, down 1.3% on Dec 19 close despite strong prior session. Broadcom's $60-90B custom AI chip TAM by 2027 remains the dominant narrative. NVDA at 130.68, holding above key support after sharp pullback from $140+ highs. The Micron miss raises questions about non-AI semiconductor demand — particularly consumer DRAM/NAND. NFLX at 90.20 (+1.4%) continues momentum ahead of NFL Christmas Day games and ad-tier growth narrative.

sections.title: Energy
sections.content: WTI crude at $69.46, essentially flat. OPEC+ delayed production unwind for the third time, pushing to Sep 2026. IEA and EIA both project well-supplied market in 2025. EIA forecasts Brent averaging $74/bbl in 2025 (down from $80 in 2024). Chinese oil demand growth stalling. Energy sector (XLE) lagging the recovery at +0.98% vs broader market. Oil services names under pressure — HAL -1.5%. The energy sector faces structural headwind of oversupply even with OPEC+ discipline, but current prices near multi-month lows provide some floor.

sections.title: Policy
sections.content: Fed policy shift is THE dominant driver. The 'hawkish cut' on Dec 18 reset the entire 2025 rate trajectory — from 4 cuts to 2. Powell flagged inflation stickiness and strong labor market. Core PCE forecast raised to 2.5%. The Nov PCE print of 2.4% (released this morning) provides modest relief, suggesting inflation may not be as sticky as feared. Government shutdown adds policy uncertainty but is likely resolved within days. Trump admin fiscal policy (tax cuts, tariffs) creates medium-term inflation risk that Fed is now explicitly pricing. Market now expects next cut not until May 2025 at earliest.

scenarios.trade: Delta is the highest-quality airline play. IATA projects $36.6B industry profit in 2025 (+16% vs 2024). Jet fuel expected at $87/bbl vs $99 in 2024. Delta's premium positioning and loyalty program generate durable revenue. Stock already showing leadership with +2.6% on Dec 19. Travel/leisure rotation is a multi-week trend, not a one-day event.

scenarios.implication: Hawkish Fed dampens consumer discretionary spending. Government shutdown disrupts TSA/FAA operations. Oil price spike from geopolitical shock. Broader market weakness drags down cyclicals.

scenarios.trade: NVDA pulled back to key support around $128-131 after the Fed shock. The AI spending narrative remains the strongest secular trend in the market. Broadcom's blowout confirmed hyperscaler demand is accelerating. Micron's weakness is NAND/consumer-specific and actually highlights the divergence between AI compute (strong) and legacy semi (weak). Triple witching may create favorable entry on any intraday dips.

scenarios.implication: Fed hawkishness compresses growth multiples. Broader tech rotation out of mega-caps. AI spending deceleration fears surface in Q1 guidance season. NVDA-specific: customer chip initiatives (AVGO custom ASICs) gradually erode GPU monopoly.

scenarios.trade: Visa is the ideal rotation trade — it benefits from consumer strength (holiday spending data strong) while being a quality compounder that holds up in volatile markets. +1.7% on Dec 19 shows relative strength. Not rate-sensitive like banks. Revenue is transaction-fee based and scales with nominal spending (inflation actually helps). In a rotation regime with uncertain direction, Visa offers asymmetric upside with limited downside.

scenarios.implication: Consumer spending rollover in Q1 2025. Government shutdown hits consumer confidence. Fintech/stablecoin competition narrative resurfaces. Broader market selloff drags down all equities.

scenarios.trade: After the massive VIX spike on the Fed day (UVXY +14%), volatility is mean-reverting hard. VIX at 18.36 and dropping, with contango term structure. SVXY benefits from both spot VIX decline and positive roll yield from contango. Post-triple-witching, realized vol typically declines into year-end (Santa Claus rally period). The cooler PCE removes the 'inflation re-acceleration' tail risk that was driving the vol spike. This is a 3-5 day mean reversion trade.

scenarios.implication: Government shutdown triggers fresh vol spike. Post-OPEX gamma flip causes renewed selling. Another macro surprise (weak data, geopolitical shock) re-ignites fear. Vol-of-vol elevated means SVXY has fat-tail risk.

scenarios.trade: Gold is catching a bid from multiple angles: dollar weakness post-PCE, haven demand from shutdown uncertainty, and a potential peak in real rates if inflation cools faster than the Fed expects. Gold was one of the best performers in 2024 driven by central bank buying and geopolitical hedging. The Dec 18 Fed shock initially hurt gold (rate-sensitive), but the cooler PCE reverses that narrative. In a rotation regime, gold offers uncorrelated returns and hedges the tail risk of shutdown or broader macro deterioration.

scenarios.implication: Dollar resumes rally if shutdown resolved quickly. Real yields rise further on strong economic data. Risk-on sentiment reduces haven demand. Year-end profit-taking in a banner year for gold.

watchlist.reason: 16% selloff after guidance miss creates potential mean-reversion opportunity if support holds at $85-87. AI memory demand (HBM) story intact but need to see selling exhaustion. Wait for stabilization before entry.
Boeing bouncing +2.6% from multi-year operational lows. Recovery narrative gaining traction but execution risk remains high. Watch for sustained above $180 to confirm trend change.
Utilities leading the bounce (+1.6%) with AI power demand as secular tailwind. Rate-sensitive so the PCE-driven rate relief helps. If 10Y yield drops below 4.45%, utilities could accelerate.
JPMorgan +1.1% showing bank leadership. Steeper yield curve (2-10 at 19bps) helps NIM. Strong capital return story. But needs broader market stability to break out above $235.

avoidList.reason: UVXY up 14% on Dec 19 but VIX already collapsing 24% pre-market. Contango + vol crush = guaranteed decay. Buying UVXY here is fighting mean reversion, contango drag, and post-OPEX vol compression. The only scenario where UVXY works is if shutdown triggers a fresh panic — low probability.

Tesla at $436 (down 0.9%) trading at extreme valuations disconnected from auto fundamentals. Musk's political involvement (government shutdown drama, DOGE) adds unpredictable headline risk. In a rotation regime, capital flows away from story stocks toward quality. Avoid until political noise subsides.

Long-duration bonds at $87.81 (down 1.5%) in a rising rate environment. The hawkish Fed dot plot structurally repriced the long end. 30Y at 4.72% may go higher as term premium rebuilds. Any shutdown resolution or strong January data would push yields even higher. Wrong side of the rate regime.
